app.xp_bekommst_du_hier_nur: Here you only earn XP for
app.zu_jeder_antwort_von_subnetting: on every answer — from subnetting through file permissions to why an average response time misleads you. Whatever you get right comes back along the forgetting curve: after one day, then three, then a week. No sign-up, everything stays on your device.
dailySub.der_baum_sucht_sich_fragen: The tree picks questions across every topic. Correct answers decide when you see the same question again.
summaryLede.noch_keine_frage_beantwortet: No question answered yet. The level rises with every correct answer — a topic you have not touched stays at level 1.
catalog.wie_software_gebaut_ausgeliefert: How software is built, shipped and observed in production. The questions cover containers, pipelines, orchestration, metrics and cloud models — the topics that separate “it runs” from “it runs reliably”.
catalog.warum_ein_container_kein_kleiner: Why a container is not a small server, what separates volumes from the container layer, and how the layer cache makes a Dockerfile fast or slow.
catalog.was_einen_build_ausloest_worin: What triggers a build, how continuous delivery differs from deployment, and why a password committed once stays in history forever.
catalog.pods_services_und_der_abgleich: Pods, services and the reconciliation of desired and actual state. Plus liveness versus readiness, and what requests and limits have to do with the OOM kill.
catalog.metrik_gegen_log_warum_p95: Metric versus log, why p95 says more than the average, what separates an SLO from an SLA, and how to spot alert fatigue.
catalog.iaas_paas_und_saas_auseinanderha: Telling IaaS, PaaS and SaaS apart, understanding the shared responsibility model, and knowing why egress drives the bill.
catalog.alles_hinter_der_oberflaeche_sch: Everything behind the interface: APIs, data storage, sign-in and the question of where validation must actually happen. Many of these come up in similar form in the German IT apprenticeship final exam for application development.
catalog.httpmethoden_und_statuscodes_was: HTTP methods and status codes, what idempotence means for a dropped connection, why versioning matters, and where a CORS error belongs fixed.
catalog.primaer_und_fremdschluessel_wher: Primary and foreign keys, WHERE versus HAVING, third normal form, ACID — and why an extra index slows a write-heavy table.
catalog.authentifizierung_gegen_autorisi: Authentication versus authorisation, hashing passwords instead of encrypting them, what never belongs in a JWT, and what makes a real second factor.
catalog.zustandsloses_http_warum_die_ein: Stateless HTTP, why browser-side validation proves nothing, parameterised queries against SQL injection, and what a reverse proxy takes off your hands.
catalog.fachlicher_schnitt_statt_technis: Slicing by domain rather than technology, one database per service, circuit breakers against cascading failure — and the honest price compared to a monolith.
catalog.was_der_nutzer_sieht_und: What the user sees and operates — and what quietly goes wrong there. From selector specificity through stacking contexts to contrast ratios and when an ARIA attribute is the wrong answer.
catalog.semantische_elemente_das_boxmode: Semantic elements, the box model with border-box, how specificity is really counted, and why a z-index of 999 sometimes does nothing at all.
catalog.let_gegen_const_die_altlast: let versus const, the typeof null legacy, why == coerces types, what really happens at an await, and what closures are for.
catalog.komponenten_und_zustandsfluss_wa: Components and state flow, why the array index as a key breaks on sorting, server versus client rendering, and the cost of global state.
catalog.was_das_viewporttag_wirklich_tut: What the viewport tag actually does, why mobile first forces a decision, minimum touch target sizes, and when container queries are the better choice.
catalog.alternativtexte_das_kontrastmini: Alt text, the 4.5:1 contrast minimum, why colour alone carries no information, what the focus ring is for, and the first rule of ARIA.
catalog.der_pruefungsschwerpunkt_der_sys: The exam focus for systems integration: OSI layers, subnetting, address ranges, firewall principles, DNS and DHCP, VLANs and wireless security. Get solid here and you can spot many faults from a single address.
catalog.osischichten_zuordnen_tcp_gegen_: Placing OSI layers, TCP versus UDP, working out host addresses from a mask, private ranges under RFC 1918, and the three-way handshake.
catalog.default_deny_als_grundhaltung_wo: Default deny as the baseline, what a DMZ is for, what a stateful firewall adds, and what it fundamentally cannot protect against.
catalog.namensaufloesung_gegen_adressver: Name resolution versus address assignment, A and CNAME records, the DORA sequence, what the TTL is for, and what a 169.254 address tells you.
catalog.mactabelle_vlantrennung_access_g: The MAC table, VLAN separation, access versus trunk ports with 802.1Q, what spanning tree protects against, and why a layer 3 switch forwards faster.
catalog.warum_wpa3_und_nicht_wep: Why WPA3 and not WEP, why only channels 1, 6 and 11 stay clear of each other, the price of the 5 GHz band, and what hiding the SSID actually achieves.
catalog.die_kommandozeile_und_der_betrie: The command line and the operations behind it: file permissions, pipes and redirection, systemd and privileges, virtualisation, backup strategies, and the measures that actually harden a system.
catalog.chmodzahlen_lesen_pipes_verkette: Reading chmod numbers, chaining pipes, the difference between > and >>, when to use find instead of grep — and what the shebang line is for.
catalog.sudo_statt_dauerroot_was_systemd: sudo instead of permanent root, what systemd manages, the principle of least privilege, group policies in Active Directory, and why no service should run as root.
catalog.hypervisor_typ_1_gegen_typ: Type 1 versus type 2 hypervisors, why a snapshot is not a backup, when overprovisioning turns against you, what live migration achieves, and when a container will do.
catalog.die_321regel_inkrementell_gegen_: The 3-2-1 rule, incremental versus differential, RTO and RPO, why only a tested restore counts, and why RAID does not replace a backup.
catalog.angriffsflaeche_verkleinern_waru: Shrinking the attack surface, why patching speed is the most effective measure, defence in depth, what full disk encryption really covers — and what it does not.
catalog.der_teil_der_in_der: The part examined in the oral discussion and needed at work every day: documenting understandably, reporting bugs usefully, finding causes instead of symptoms, estimating honestly, and speaking up in time.
catalog.was_in_eine_uebergabe_gehoert: What belongs in a handover, why a training-log entry has to be concrete, when a comment earns its place, and why outdated documentation is worse than none.
catalog.wozu_ein_standup_wirklich_da: What a standup is actually for, what a code review should achieve, what usable feedback looks like, and what psychological safety changes.
catalog.erst_reproduzieren_dann_aendern_: Reproduce first, then change. What a usable bug report contains, how the five whys lead to the root cause, and why you change only one thing at a time.
catalog.mit_dem_problem_anfangen_statt: Starting with the problem rather than the architecture, not reading slides aloud, handling questions you cannot answer, and what belongs in the discussion about your project.
catalog.wichtig_gegen_dringend_warum_ein: Important versus urgent, why a range is more honest than a single number, what starting things in parallel costs, and when a delay has to be reported.
lernsystem.der_baum_misst_nicht_wie: The tree does not measure how often you pressed a button, but what you can answer. That is why there is no way to award yourself XP here — every point comes from a correct answer or from work you documented in your training log.
lernsystem.eine_runde_sind_zehn_fragen: A round is ten questions. The tree takes everything due for review today first and tops up the rest from the topics you have covered least.
lernsystem.auch_die_richtige_die_erklaer: The correct one too. The explanation says not only what is right, but why the other three options are wrong — that is the part that carries you through an exam.
lernsystem.richtig_beantwortet_heisst_di: Answered correctly means the question returns later, at growing intervals. Answered incorrectly means it comes back within the same round and the interval starts over.
lernsystem.jedes_thema_hat_grundlagen_fo: Every topic has basics, advanced and pro. The next tier opens once the one below is solid — not after a set time and not after a set number of attempts.
beispielfragen.sechs_fragen_im_wortlaut_: Six questions verbatim, one per subject area — so you can see what you are getting into before the first click. The correct answer is right below each one.
beispielfragen.was_unterscheidet_einen_c: What separates a container from a virtual machine?
beispielfragen.container_haben_kein_eige: Containers have no file system of their own
beispielfragen.eine_vm_bringt_ein_komple: A VM ships a full guest operating system with its own kernel. A container uses the host kernel and only isolates processes, network and file system — which is why it starts in seconds instead of minutes.
beispielfragen.welches_sqlschluesselwort: Which SQL keyword filters rows before grouping?
beispielfragen.where_filtert_einzelne_ze: WHERE filters individual rows before grouping. HAVING filters afterwards on the groups — which is why HAVING may use aggregate functions such as COUNT and WHERE may not.
beispielfragen.welches_kontrastverhaeltn: What contrast ratio does WCAG require at minimum for normal body text?
beispielfragen.stufe_aa_verlangt_451_fue: Level AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text from 18.66 px bold or 24 px regular. Controls and graphics also need at least 3:1 against their background.
beispielfragen.wie_viele_nutzbare_hostad: How many usable host addresses does a /29 network have?
beispielfragen.29_laesst_3_hostbits_also: /29 leaves 3 host bits, so 2 to the power of 3 equals 8 addresses. Network address and broadcast drop out, leaving 6 usable. The rule of thumb is 2^(32 minus prefix) minus 2.
beispielfragen.was_bewirkt_chmod_755_auf: What does chmod 755 do to a file?
beispielfragen.eigentuemer_alles_gruppe_: Owner everything, group and others read and execute
beispielfragen.die_ziffern_stehen_fuer_e: The digits stand for owner, group and others. 7 is 4+2+1 meaning read, write, execute; 5 is 4+1 meaning read and execute. On directories the execute bit means the right to enter.
beispielfragen.was_ist_der_erste_sinnvol: What is the first sensible step on a reported bug?
beispielfragen.was_nicht_reproduzierbar_: What cannot be reproduced cannot be verifiably fixed. First establish the exact steps, inputs and environment — otherwise you repair something and afterwards do not know whether it helped.
faq.kostet_der_skillbaum_etwas_und: Does the skill tree cost anything and do I need an account?
faq.nein_und_nein_alle_150: No and no. All 150 questions are freely available, there is no sign-up and no paywall. Your progress lives in your browser storage and never leaves this device — nothing is uploaded anywhere. The flip side: on another device, or after clearing your browser data, you start from zero.
faq.nicht_mehr_bis_version_646: Not any more. Up to version 6.4.6 there was a button for it — but a number you type in yourself says nothing about knowledge. XP now comes from correct answers and from work documented in your training log. A level is therefore a statement about what you can answer, not about how generous you were.
faq.was_bedeutet_wiederholung_nach_der: What does review along the forgetting curve mean?
faq.neu_gelerntes_wissen_zerfaellt_schne: Newly learned knowledge decays fast; repeated knowledge decays far more slowly. So every correct answer sets when the same question comes back: after one day, then three, then a week, and so on. A wrong answer resets the interval and the question reappears within the same round.
faq.der_praktische_effekt_zehn_minuten: The practical effect: ten minutes a day beats two hours at the weekend — and you automatically practise whatever you are just starting to forget.
faq.ersetzt_der_skillbaum_die_vorbereitu: Does the skill tree replace preparing for the chamber exam?
faq.nein_die_fragen_liegen_auf: No. The questions sit at apprenticeship level and cover many final-exam topics, but they are not official exam papers and not a complete syllabus. For the exam itself you also need the curriculum for your occupation, your vocational school material and practice papers from your chamber. The tree is the daily repetition in between.
faq.wofuer_sind_level_und_xp: What are levels and XP in the skill tree for?
faq.xp_misst_aufwand_wie_viel: XP measures effort: how much you have answered correctly in a topic. The level is derived from it and deliberately grows more slowly the higher it gets. Neither says whether you will retain a topic — that is what the review preview on the progress card is for, showing how many questions fall due over the coming days.
faq.was_hat_das_berichtsheft_mit: What does the training log have to do with the skill tree?
faq.wenn_du_deine_taetigkeiten_in: If you record your work in
faq.festhaeltst_kann_der_baum_diese: the tree can analyse those entries and credit the topics it recognises with XP — documented practice counts just like answered questions. The analysis runs entirely in your browser against a keyword list; nothing is sent anywhere and no AI is consulted.
faq.wie_viele_fragen_gibt_es: How many questions are there per topic?
faq.fuenf_je_thema_verteilt_auf: Five per topic, spread across three tiers: two basics, two advanced, one pro. Across 30 topics that is 150 questions. Because every question keeps falling due over months, the set lasts considerably longer than the number suggests.
weiter.wochenberichte_schreiben_drucken_: Write and print weekly reports and export them on the official chamber form — the basis for the analysis here.
weiter.fachrichtungen_ablauf_der_ausbild: Specialisms, how the apprenticeship runs, and what parts 1 and 2 of the final exam actually test.
weiter.lange_erklaerstuecke_mit_bedienba: Long explainers with interactive diagrams — how memory forgets, how an SSD ages, how a qubit computes.
weiter.wiederkehrende_aufgaben_im_ausbil: Keep track of recurring tasks in your working day and tick them off.
scanBackdrop.sucht_in_deinen_berichtshef: Searches your training-log entries and notes for technical terms and credits the topics it recognises as XP. The analysis runs in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere. Each entry counts only once.
